mig_27k: The MiG-27K was Mikoyan's fully upgraded version of the swing-wing MiG-27 strike jet, built around the Kayra-23 laser-optical sight so it could use laser- and TV-guided weapons; its cost led the Soviet Air Force to halve the order and fill the rest with the cheaper MiG-27M. In mixed battles that sight and a large stock of guided ordnance make ground targets easy prey. It is useful in air battles too, with enough bombs for a base, a full set of air-to-air missiles and the lively low-level handling known from the MiG-27M. It arrived with the "Winged Lions" update.
mig_27m: Developed after the MiG-27K as a cheaper partner for it, the MiG-27M kept the ability to use laser- and TV-guided weapons but swapped the costly Kayra-23 for a targeting system borrowed from the Su-17 family, and it served with the USSR and several export users through the 1980s. It gives the Soviet bomber line its first guided weapons, and together with the six-barrel GSh-6-30 cannon they let it hit ground targets precisely in mixed battles. Built on the MiG-23BN airframe and carrying R-13M1 and R-60M missiles plus plenty of large countermeasures, it can still look after itself in a dogfight. It came in Update "Direct Hit".
mig_29_9_12: Mikoyan's light frontline fighter was conceived in the 1970s to work alongside the larger Su-27 and replace the MiG-23; it first flew in October 1977, and the 9-12 production model reached units in 1983, designed to be fast, agile and easy to maintain from rough airfields, though short on range. In the game this early model pairs high top speed and strong acceleration with good handling, plus a capable radar and helmet sight for cueing short- and medium-range missiles. It misses the better missiles of later Fulcrums, its R-60Ms are easily decoyed by flares and it has little to use on ground targets. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
mig_29_9_12_germany: East Germany bought 24 export-standard MiG-29 9-12A fighters in the 1980s, and after reunification the Luftwaffe kept them for more than a decade; a 1994 exercise against USAF F-16s at Aviano showed NATO how badly it had underrated the type, and in 2003 22 of them went to Poland for one euro apiece. In the German tree it follows the MiG-23MLA and opens the fourth-generation era, bringing the strong R-27ER1 radar missile and a helmet-mounted sight for off-boresight shots with its all-aspect IR missiles. It came with Update 2.25 "Sky Guardians".
mig_29_9_12_sniper: Romania's MiG-29 Sniper was an upgrade programme that would have given its Fulcrums Western avionics, including colour multifunction displays, a new HUD and an Elisra SPS-20(V) radar warning receiver, while keeping Soviet weapons; it was cancelled in favour of the MiG-21 LanceR. Sold as a premium pack in the Italian tree since the "Leviathans" update, it uses R-27ER missiles at longer range, R-60Ms up close and a helmet sight for off-boresight locks, and its digital RWR gives clear track and launch warnings. The usual Fulcrum weaknesses remain: the N019E radar trails NATO rivals, and it holds energy poorly, leaving it exposed to F-15s and F-16s in a turning fight.
mig_29_9_12b_hungary: Hungary received 28 MiG-29s of the 9-12B standard in 1993 as part of Russia's debt settlement, a big step up from its worn MiG-23MFs; after joining NATO in 1999 it moved to the Gripen and retired its last Fulcrum in December 2010. It sits in the Hungarian part of the Italian tree, following the MiG-23MF, and flies quite differently from the F-16A ADF at the same stage. Its main tools are the R-27ER1 radar missile and a helmet-mounted sight for aiming all-aspect IR missiles off-boresight. It arrived in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
mig_29_9_12g: After reunification the Luftwaffe kept its ex-East German MiG-29s, which had outperformed most NATO fighters in testing, and upgraded them as the MiG-29G with Western avionics and NATO-compatible communications and navigation. In the game it flies much like the older 9-12 but adds R-27ET1 and R-73E missiles, making it a lighter alternative to the MiG-29SMT. It goes without the SMT's guided ground weapons, extra countermeasures, fuel and newer radar, but also avoids the weight that makes that version so sluggish. It was introduced in the "Kings of Battle" update.
mig_29_9_13: Shaped by Soviet lessons that agile fighters still mattered, Mikoyan's Fulcrum first flew in October 1977 with twin engines, a strong radar and a helmet-mounted sight for close combat; the 9-13 entered production in 1986 with a larger fuel bulge behind the cockpit and reshaped wingtips. When added in Update "Apex Predators" it became the Soviet tree's first fourth-generation fighter, and it plays almost exactly like the 9-12. A true pulse-Doppler radar, the excellent R-27ER and a helmet sight that cues R-60M and R-27T missiles off-boresight give it far more options than the MiG-23 before it.
mig_29kr_9_41r: The carrier-based MiG-29K, derived from the MiG-29M, first landed on the carrier now called Admiral Kuznetsov in 1989 but was shelved after the Soviet collapse; revived by an Indian order, it returned for the Russian Navy, which contracted 20 single-seat MiG-29KRs in 2012 and used them against targets in Syria in 2016. Compared with the MiG-29M it has a larger wing and more powerful engines. Kh-31A/P and TV-guided Kh-29 missiles make it effective against ground targets, while R-77s and R-73s cover air combat, though it cannot carry R-27s. It was added in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
mig_29m_9_15: A deep redesign of the Fulcrum begun in the mid-1980s, the MiG-29M gained a reworked airframe with more fuel, fly-by-wire controls and the N010 Zhuk radar, opening up R-77 missiles and precision strike weapons; six prototypes flew, but early-1990s budget cuts stopped production, and the design fed into the MiG-29K and MiG-35. In the game it can carry as many as eight R-77s, and RD-33K engines help offset the heavier airframe. Up to four TV-guided Kh-29TD missiles cover ground work, though it has no targeting pod and few flares. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
mig_29n: Malaysia ordered 18 MiG-29s in 1994, took delivery in 1995 and later upgraded them locally towards the 9.12SD standard with in-flight refuelling, a better radar and RVV-AE missiles; they served until 2017, when the Su-30MKM replaced them. In the Japanese tree it plays as an early Fulcrum with active radar-homing RVV-AE missiles added, backed by high top speed, strong acceleration and good handling from its powerful engines. The avionics are dated, and against armour it has only rockets, napalm and unguided bombs. It came in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
mig_29smt_9_19: With Russia's next-generation fighter programmes stalled for lack of money, RSK MiG revived its 1990s MiG-29SMT modernisation as a cheaper answer to late F-16s and the new European canard fighters; the 9-19 standard was finalised in 2006 and serves with Russia, Algeria and Syria. It flies noticeably worse than the MiG-29 (9-13), but it carries far stronger weapons, headed by R-77 missiles, along with improved avionics and radar and a wider choice of guided ground ordnance for precise strikes. It was added in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila".
mig_35: A "4++ generation" development of the MiG-29M and MiG-29K, the MiG-35 adds an AESA radar, a new helmet display and more guided strike weapons; it first flew in January 2017, and the first two production jets were delivered in 2019. In the game it climbs well, is quick at altitude and uses its radar and helmet sight to employ R-77-1 and R-73 missiles at short and medium range. Kh-38ML/MT missiles and guided bombs make it a strong mixed-battle aircraft, and its subsonic handling equals the best Fulcrums, but its limited fuel needs careful management. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
mig_3_series_1_15: Designed by Mikoyan-Gurevich as a high-altitude interceptor, the MiG-3 could outpace the Bf 109 at around 6,000 m, though its AM-35A engine left it slower near sea level. In the game it is one of the first fighters able to reach high-flying bombers, and it works best climbing early and diving on targets below rather than turning, as its controls are stiff and it is less agile than its rivals. The centrally mounted armament of one 12.7 mm and two 7.62 mm machine guns needs no convergence but is weak, so hits must land on the pilot, engine or fuel tanks. It was added in Update 1.31.
mig_3_series_1_15_bk_pod: This MiG-3-15 variant differs from the standard aircraft only in two extra non-synchronised 12.7 mm Berezin UB guns, giving it three UBs and two 7.62 mm ShKAS behind a 1,200 hp Mikulin AM-35A. No other plane in the game uses more Berezin UBs as its main armament; the gun fires faster and with higher muzzle velocity than the American M2 Browning, and short bursts aimed at wings or engines bring down light fighters, though bombers soak up hits better. Like the base MiG-3 it is an energy fighter suited to boom-and-zoom, quite unlike the I-16 line before it. It arrived in Update 1.37.
mig_3_series_34: An experimental MiG-3 variant meant to fix the series' weak firepower, the MiG-3-34 came from a high-altitude design that struggled in service with poor build quality and oxygen supply, and in 1941 it met agile Bf 109s instead of bombers before Yak and LaGG fighters replaced it. In the game it relies on good top speed and acceleration, much like the I-185 and I-225. It cannot out-turn or outgun Spitfires and Bf 109s, so it does best climbing above 4,000 m, where its engine reaches full output, speed matters more than agility and enemy bombers are found. It arrived in Update 1.41.
mirage_2000_5eg_mk2_greece: Greece ordered 40 Mirage 2000s in 1985 and in the early 2000s upgraded part of the fleet and bought 15 more to the 2000-5 Mk.2 standard, with RDY-2 radar, modern avionics and MICA missiles; the Rafale is now replacing them. In the Israeli tree it is functionally the same as the French Mirage 2000-5F: the delta wing gives excellent agility and the engine plenty of speed, with R550 Magic 2 missiles for close range and MICA-EM for medium range. It bleeds energy fast in sustained turns, and anti-radiation missiles are its only air-to-ground option. It was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
mirage_2000_5ei: Taiwan's air force, unable to buy F-4s or F-16s from the US in the 1980s to replace ageing F-104s and F-5s, turned to France and received Mirage 2000-5Ei fighters from 1997 with ground-attack capability removed; the deal helped push Washington into selling F-16s from 1998. In the Chinese tree it is essentially a single-seat Mirage 2000-5F without strike weapons. It lacks the long-range missiles to trade well with F-15Es or J-10As, but its strong electronics and MICA-EM missiles make it effective at picking off surviving enemies late in a match. It arrived in Update "Firebirds".
mirage_2000_5f: Dassault's Mirage 2000-5F, first flown in 1991, brought upgraded avionics and weapons to the Mirage 2000 line and flew both air-to-air and ground-attack sorties over Kosovo in 1999. In the game its strength is air combat: the infrared-guided Matra Magic 2 deals well with close-range targets, the Thales RDY radar picks up and tracks several targets quickly, and the airframe's agility helps it win positions in a dogfight. It came to the game in the "La Royale" update.
mirage_2000c_s4: Dassault's Mirage 2000 first flew in 1978 after the AFVG and Mirage G projects failed, and the C ("Chasseur") version long served as France's main interceptor. The C-S4 arrived in Update "Air Superiority" as a reward from the 2023 Winter Extreme event and is nearly identical to the tech-tree C-S5, but has fewer countermeasures and no missile approach warning. It plays the same way, using strong flight performance, all-aspect R.550 Magic 2 missiles and Super 530D radar missiles to pick its fights.
mirage_2000c_s5: The penultimate Mirage 2000C standard added the uprated M53-P2 engine, an Eclair chaff and flare dispenser and the improved RDI radar for the Super 530D missile, bringing it level with contemporary MiG-29s and F-16s. In the game it carries fewer missiles and bombs than its rivals but has a powerful engine in a light airframe: quick acceleration, high top speed and a good angle of attack, and although the delta bleeds energy at low speed it regains it fast. Its 530Ds trail late AIM-7s and R-27s at long range, so it fights best low down, using the IRCCM-equipped Magic 2 inside about 3 km. It arrived in Update "Drone Age".
mirage_2000d_r1: Descended from the nuclear-strike Mirage 2000N by way of the 2000D, the D-R1 is a two-seat ground-attack Mirage with improved countermeasures, ECM and RWR, plus AS-30L missiles, laser-guided bombs and a targeting pod. Its precise weapons come in small numbers: two GBU-12s and two AS-30Ls at once, alongside two Magic 2 missiles. The heavier two-seat airframe keeps the 2000C's strong engine, giving good low-speed acceleration and a high top speed but heavy fuel use. It suits ground battles best, bombing from height and then using the AS-30L, whose HE warhead is better against distant SPAA than tanks; it arrived in Update "Apex Predators".
mirage_2000d_rmv: Dassault's mid-life renovation programme, launched in 2015, gave the strike Mirage new avionics and a wider range of weapons, with upgraded aircraft reaching units from 2022 and 55 planned to keep the type flying into the 2030s. Compared with the D-R1, the RMV adds GBU-48, GBU-49 and GBU-50 bombs with combined satellite and laser guidance and the DAMOCLES targeting pod, while keeping the older weapons. It remains a dedicated attacker with little to offer in air combat. It came in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
mirage_3c: The first production Mirage III, the IIIC was a delta-wing interceptor and dogfighter with an afterburning Atar 09B, DEFA 30 mm cannons and, at first, AIM-9B Sidewinders; 95 were built and it served until 1988. In the game it brings a strong engine, 30 mm guns and a radar best used at high altitude, armed with Magic 1 and R530E missiles. The weak radar limits the R530 to high altitude, acceleration is mediocre and it has no flares, so it relies on keeping speed and firing Magic 1s inside about 2 km. It arrived in Update "Starfighters".
mirage_3cj: The Shahak was Israel's Mirage IIICJ and its first Mach 2 fighter, the main air superiority aircraft through the Six-Day and Yom Kippur wars, where pilots often trusted the DEFA cannons over unreliable missiles; 72 served before the Kfir and F-4 took over. It flies much like the French Mirage IIIC but carries American AIM-9Ds instead of Magic 1s. Agile with a high angle of attack, it sheds energy quickly when turning and accelerates poorly at low speed, and with no countermeasures, speed is its main defence. It came with the "Winged Lions" update.
mirage_3e: Built as a more multirole partner to the interceptor Mirage IIIC, the IIIE added a British pulse-Doppler navigation radar under the cockpit, more fuel, a newer ATAR 09 engine and better avionics; with 192 built for the French Air Force, it was the most produced Mirage III by 1971. In the game a ballistic computer helps it hit ground targets with guns, bombs and rockets, and its updated Atar 9 is a little stronger and much quicker to respond. It also gains an RWR and a countermeasure dispenser over the IIIC. It arrived in Update "Ixwa Strike".
mirage_3s_c70_switzerland: Switzerland chose the Mirage IIIC as its first supersonic fighter and built it under licence as the Mirage IIIS, though funding cut production from 100 to 54; from 1988 the fleet gained canards (C.70 stands for "canard wing at 70%") and new avionics, and most retired in 1999. In the German tree it has better avionics than the French IIIC, SARH AIM-26 missiles and a licence-built AIM-9E, and can use the SEPR844 rocket booster as well as new JATO rockets. It loses speed heavily when manoeuvring and carries no air-to-ground weapons. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
mirage_4000: Dassault's private-venture Mirage 4000, essentially a twin-engined, canard-equipped Mirage 2000 scaled up to rival the F-15, found no buyer: France judged it too expensive and export prospects fell through, so the single prototype ended up in the Paris Air and Space Museum in 1992, its lessons passing to the Rafale. In the game it handles nearly every job, pairing excellent dogfighting with up to eight Magic 2s, up to four Super 530Ds guided by a strong radar, and the ATLIS pod with laser-guided bombs and missiles for ground attack. It came in Update "Air Superiority" and builds on the earlier Mirage 2000s.
mirage_5ba: Belgium ordered Mirage 5s in 1968 to replace its F-84F and RF-84F jets, with 54 of the planned 88 being Mirage 5BA fighters fitted with American electronics; after the Cold War 20 were sold to Chile as the Elkan. In the French tree it is an agile fighter with good missiles, but it carries few of them, has little cannon ammunition and no guided air-to-ground weapons. Unlike the French Mirage 5F, it has countermeasures. It came in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
mirage_5f: The Mirage 5 was a stripped-down Mirage III requested by Israel, trading radar and avionics for extra fuel; France's 1967 arms embargo blocked delivery of the 50 ordered, and Israel, after taking a refund, built its own copy, the Nesher, from blueprints obtained through espionage. In the game it matches the Nesher except for armament, using AIM-9Bs and Magic 1s instead of Shafrir 2s. With no radar, only two short-range missiles and no countermeasures, it suits a defensive style: staying clear of all-aspect missile carriers, bombing bases and using its speed to catch unwary targets. It came in the "Winged Lions" update.
